verifications.claim: Google Messages is updating to allow partial text selection.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Google Messages is now rolling out the ability to copy only parts of a message" (R1); "Users can now long-press a message and select portions of the text to copy" (R2); "the app is rolling out the ability to select and copy only part of a message" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: All references directly confirm the update adds partial text selection/copy in Google Messages.

verifications.claim: Partial text selection in Google Messages was spotted in beta version v20260306.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Starting with Google Messages v20260306 beta" (R1); "version v20260306" (R3); "Google Messages v20260306 beta" (R4, R5); "recent beta builds of Google Messages" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly link the feature to beta version v20260306.

verifications.claim: In Google Messages beta version v20260306, users can long-press a message and drag to select text.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "long-press a message and drag to highlight a specific portion of the text" (R1); "drag selection handles across the text" (R3); "long-press a message and then drag to select a specific part" (R4, R5); "drag handles to highlight exactly what you want" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly describe long-press and drag in v20260306 beta.

verifications.claim: In Google Messages beta version v20260306, users can use the traditional full-copy button.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "tap the existing “Copy” option in the message menu" (R1); "still use the “copy” button to grab the entire message" (R2); "the full-message “Copy” action remains" (R3); "the “Copy” button isn’t going anywhere" (R4); "tap on the “Copy” button" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm the full-copy button remains available alongside partial selection in the beta.

verifications.claim: Users can highlight specific text within a message bubble (OTP codes, phone numbers, addresses) instead of copying the entire text string.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "OTP codes, links, and addresses" (R5); "OTPs buried in disclaimers, addresses wrapped in marketing text" (R3); "OTPs, links, or addresses" (R4); "copy entire messages, especially ones with courier tracking numbers" (R1)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly mention highlighting specifics like OTPs, addresses instead of full text.

verifications.claim: Users long-press a message and use the updated context sheet to select text.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "long-press a message and drag to highlight" (R1); "long-press a message, the usual menu will appear. Now... highlight and select specific parts" (R2); "Long-press a message bubble... drag selection handles... A toolbar appears" (R3); "true text selection within the long-press context sheet" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Direct descriptions of long-press leading to context sheet/toolbar for text selection.

verifications.claim: The standard "Copy" button remains available for copying everything, notes Android Police.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "If you use the Copy option directly from the long-press menu, the app will still copy the entire message" (R8, Android Police); "the “Copy” button isn’t going anywhere" (R4); "tap on the “Copy” button to do so" (R5)
verifications.reasoning: Android Police (R8) and others confirm standard Copy button for full text remains.

verifications.claim: The partial text selection feature in Google Messages is currently available in a staged rollout to users in the Google Messages beta program (v20260306).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "staged rollout, with some beta users seeing the change" (R3); "staged rollout, as this feature doesn’t seem to be available for everyone" (R4, R5); "staged rollout to certain users" (R7); "staged rollout" (R6)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources specify staged rollout in v20260306 beta.

verifications.claim: The partial text selection change in Google Messages removes the need for workarounds like pasting full messages into other apps to delete unnecessary parts.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "instead of forcing you to copy the whole thing and then paste it somewhere else" (R1); "copy the entire message into a notes app... and then copy only the specific portion" (R2); "copy the full message, paste it into another app, and manually delete" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: All sources highlight elimination of workarounds like pasting to other apps.

verifications.claim: The Google Messages update is designed to behave like Android's standard system-level text selection, say this article.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The experience feels consistent with Android’s system-level text selection, which should reduce mis-taps and make the action second nature." (R6)
verifications.reasoning: R6 directly states consistency with Android's system-level text selection.
